text: Partition circles and rectangles into two and four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, fourths, and quarters, and use the phrases half of, fourth of, and quarter of. Describe the whole as two of, or four of the shares. Understand for these examples that decomposing into more equal shares creates smaller shares.

learning_components.text: Describe a whole as four quarters or four fourths
Describe a whole as two halves
Partition circles and rectangles into four equal shares, and describe the shares using the words fourths and quarters and the phrases fourth of and quarter of
Partition circles and rectangles into two equal shares, and describe the shares using the word halves and the phrase half of
Recognize that decomposing a shape into fourths creates smaller shares than decomposing that same shape into halves

text: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit) end to end; understand that the length measurement of an object is the number of same-size length units that span it with no gaps or overlaps.

learning_components.text: Express the length of an object as a whole number of length units, by laying multiple copies of a shorter object (the length unit, such as a paperclip) end to end.
Know that to measure the length of an object with a number of same-size length units, the units must span the object with no gaps or overlaps

text: Partition circles and rectangles into two, three, or four equal shares, describe the shares using the words halves, thirds, half of, a third of, etc., and describe the whole as two halves, three thirds, four fourths. Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape.

learning_components.text: Describe a whole based on its number of parts, including two halves, three thirds, and four fourths
Partition objects, including circles and rectangles, into four equal shares and describe the shares using "fourths"
Partition objects, including circles and rectangles, into three equal shares and describe the shares using "thirds"
Partition objects, including circles and rectangles, into two equal shares and describe the shares using "halves"
Recognize that equal shares of identical wholes need not have the same shape

text: Represent whole numbers as lengths from 0 on a number line diagram with equally spaced points corresponding to the numbers 0, 1, 2, …, and represent whole-number sums and differences within 100 on a number line diagram.

learning_components.text: Represent whole numbers as lengths on a number line diagram
Represent whole-number differences on a number line diagram
Represent whole-number sums and differences on a number line diagram
Represent whole-number sums on a number line diagram

text: Partition shapes into parts with equal areas. Express the area of each part as a unit fraction of the whole. *For example, partition a shape into 4 parts with equal area, and describe the area of each part as $\frac{1}{4}$ of the area of the shape.*

learning_components.text: Express the area of each equal part of a shape as a unit fraction of the whole (with denominators of 2, 3, 4, 6, and 8)
Partition shapes into parts with equal areas (2, 3, 4, 6, or 8 equal parts)

text: Interpret products of whole numbers, e.g., interpret $5 \times 7$ as the total number of objects in 5 groups of 7 objects each. *For example, describe a context in which a total number of objects can be expressed as $5 \div 7$.*

learning_components.text: Identify a multiplication situation based on a given multiplication expression
Identify a multiplication situation based on a given multiplication expression (up to and including 10x10)
Interpret the product of two whole numbers (up to and including 10x10) as the number of groups times the size of each group, or vice versa
Interpret the product of two whole numbers as the number of groups times the size of each group, or vice versa
Model a multiplication situation (up to and including 10x10), including by writing a multiplication expression
Model a multiplication situation, including by writing a multiplication expression

text: Interpret whole-number quotients of whole numbers, e.g., interpret $56 \div 8$ as the number of objects in each share when 56 objects are partitioned equally into 8 shares, or as a number of shares when 56 objects are partitioned into equal shares of 8 objects each. *For example, describe a context in which a number of shares or a number of groups can be expressed as $56 \div 8$.*

learning_components.text: Identify a division situation (limited to dividends through 50 and divisors and quotients through 10) based on a given division expression
Identify a division situation based on a given division expression
Interpret whole number quotients as the number of groups when a set number of objects is partitioned into equal groups
Interpret whole number quotients as the number of groups when a set number of objects is partitioned into equal groups (limited to dividends through 50 and divisors and quotients through 10)
Interpret whole number quotients as the number of objects in each group when a set number of objects is partitioned into equal groups

Interpret whole number quotients as the number of objects in each group when a set number of objects is partitioned into equal groups (limited to dividends through 50 and divisors and quotients through 10)
Model a division situation (limited to dividends through 50 and divisors and quotients through 10), including by writing a division expression
Model a division situation, including by writing a division expression

text: Understand division as an unknown-factor problem. *For example, find $32 \div 8$ by finding the number that makes 32 when multiplied by 8.*

learning_components.text: Determine a quotient by representing a division problem as an equivalent multiplication problem
Represent a division problem as an equivalent multiplication problem with an unknown factor
